anwen.greet: You have both feet under you. A good beginning.
anwen.reassure: Then stay long enough to listen. We needn't solve everything at once.
anwen.work: Clean linen first. Questions after the patient has water.
anwen.apology: Thank you. Keep the doorway clear; someone may need it quickly.

rook.greet: There you are. I was beginning to owe somebody an explanation.
rook.joke: My prices are perfectly honest. My stories enjoy a little more freedom.
rook.reassure: Company helps. Advice is charged separately. That was a joke.
rook.work: Check the fastening underneath. The one everyone forgets until the road remembers.
rook.apology: No harm to the satchel. We'll call that an improvement.

mira.greet: Mind the stems by your boot. They have had a difficult enough morning.
mira.joke: That plant will cure nothing except an appetite for bad advice.
mira.reassure: You can help without promising the weather will improve.
mira.work: Sound leaves here, damp ones apart. Drying is not the same as hiding rot.
mira.apology: Room to work is apology enough. Thank you.

tor.greet: Come round where I can see you. Hot iron doesn't wait for introductions.
tor.joke: If the stool complains, tighten it. Same cure seldom works on Rook.
tor.reassure: Hold the useful end. We'll find out what the joint can bear.
tor.work: Look for the bright wear beside the pin. That tells you where the load really goes.
tor.apology: Right. Clear of the swing now.

elna.greet: There's room beside the basket. Not on it.
elna.reassure: Sit a moment, then. You don't have to improve the silence.
elna.work: I'm keeping the sound cloth. A patched thing can still be worth keeping.
elna.apology: A little space. That's all I asked.

toma.greet: Dry ground on this side. I've already tested the other with my boots.
toma.joke: The crows know the planting schedule better than I do.
toma.reassure: One useful thing before supper. That usually helps.
toma.work: The shallow run feeds the beds. Clearing it is different from digging it deeper.
toma.apology: Good. I'd rather mend a fence than an argument.

senn.greet: Keep your hands where we can see them. Then speak.
senn.work: Count the people through, not just the loads. That is what a watch is for.
senn.apology: Keep the weapon down. We can hear you without it.

edric.greet: You have my attention. Use it plainly.
edric.work: The stores must feed people before an argument about authority can feed anyone.
edric.apology: Then let us continue without the display.

vale.greet: A moment. I will mark the line rather than pretend I remember it.
vale.joke: My index has no entry for a short, uncomplicated complaint. A surprising omission.
vale.reassure: Keep the source with the claim. That is something we can actually do.
vale.work: A witness's words belong beside their limits. A clean copy must keep both.
vale.apology: Thank you. The paper need not suffer for the conversation.

merrow.greet: Which matter? I would rather find the right page first.
merrow.work: An answer needs a destination. Otherwise it is just another signed sheet.
merrow.apology: Leave the passage open and we can begin again.

nessa.greet: Hot side of the tray. Other side of the argument.
nessa.joke: The small loaf is not a shortage. It's the one I dropped. There, a trade secret.
nessa.reassure: Set out another bowl. Worry does less harm with something to do.
nessa.work: Weigh before you divide. Generosity that forgets the last household isn't generous.
nessa.apology: No one burned? Then give me room and we'll survive it.

nera.greet: Check the strap before leaning on the cart.
nera.joke: The cart has fewer opinions than the crew. More reliable brakes, too.
nera.reassure: You can take the next useful job. That's enough for now.
nera.work: The load is tied to survive a turn, not to look tidy while standing still.
nera.apology: Keep the approach clear. People need a way through.

rumours.claim: Rook has heard that a missing grain sack was taken at the village scale. He did not see it happen.
rumours.finding: The grain work has been resolved. Its recorded outcome, not Rook's suspicion, is the surviving account.

rumours.claim: Toma has heard that all the water is poisoned. He has seen disturbed silt, not tested every stream.
rumours.finding: The surveyed watercourse and completed work establish a local problem and response, not an evil forest.

rumours.claim: Nessa has heard that every delayed load went into the old mill. Her own missing delivery does not prove that.
rumours.finding: The second-ledger work records what could actually be traced. It cannot account for every lost delivery.

rumours.claim: Rook has heard that every toll was ordered from the Castle. He has no signed order for that claim.
rumours.finding: The toll inquiry establishes its recorded responsibility; a uniform alone never established who ordered it.

rumours.claim: Vale has received a claim that every altered line came from one hand. Matching ink is not identification.
rumours.finding: The compared orders distinguish surviving alterations from claims about their author.

rumours.claim: Mira has heard that nothing will grow after the covenant changes. No one has watched that future yet.
rumours.finding: The completed growing work is something witnessed after the decision, not a guarantee about every future season.

objects.title: Tor's working hammer
objects.text: Three small notches identify the maker. Bright metal at one edge shows how Tor favors the face. He has offered the tool for examination, not given it away.

objects.title: Mira's seed case
objects.text: The lid slides across the grain instead of against it. Dry chaff sits in the finger notch. This is a working container, not a promise that every seed will grow.

objects.title: A folded delivery letter
objects.text: A fold worn almost through, a seal still whole. Nessa permits Kael to examine the outside. The private words stay folded.

objects.title: Nera's practice knot
objects.text: Two loaded turns grip together; the free end can still be found by touch. A knot serves the people crossing, not the person claiming the road.

objects.title: The counter seal
objects.text: The short stroke below the main mark distinguishes an acknowledged copy. The tool alone proves neither permission nor the truth of a page.

objects.title: A clasp kept for repair
objects.text: The pin is iron, the loop brass: replace the worn part rather than throw both away. Tor has kept it for its owner, not for a museum.

favours.request: Leave one loaf for the next patient
favours.reply: I'll keep it covered. Take this old linen clasp; it catches on the clean cloth, but it has held a great deal together.
favours.title: Anwen's retired linen clasp

favours.request: Share one sound bitterleaf for the drying rack
favours.reply: Sound all the way to the stem. Here: an empty seed case. Better in use than forgotten in my basket.
favours.title: Mira's empty seed case

favours.request: Leave one scrap iron for a replacement pin
favours.reply: Enough for the joint. You can keep the old test piece. It never held a building up, but it taught me where the fault was.
favours.title: Tor's worn test piece

favours.request: Share a loaf with the crossing crew
favours.reply: I'll split it between the two still working. This short knot is spare; pull the turns apart when you want to learn how it holds.
favours.title: Nera's short practice knot

favours.request: Leave one loaf for the waiting servants
favours.reply: No one has to give testimony for a meal. Keep the empty delivery sleeve; the names inside are mine to protect.
favours.title: Nessa's empty delivery sleeve

favours.request: Lend one scrap iron for the cart fastening
favours.reply: That will hold. Take my retired counting stamp. No value in it except the journeys; don't let anyone charge you for those.
favours.title: Rook's retired counting stamp
